description:
Route `BitMatrix::matvec` through AVX2-dispatched popcount machinery at the A1 dense design sizes.

## Background

`BitMatrix::matvec` computes parity per row with scalar `(row_word & x_word).count_ones() % 2`. The SIMD dispatch bundle was already available through `gf2_core::simd::maybe_simd()`, but this path did not use it.

The original routing-only design attempted to reduce each row using existing logical kernels and then call `popcnt_fn`. Lead review rejected the first implementation because its 512/1024-column speedup came from scalar ILP fallback instead of SIMD routing. The user then approved a scope amendment for R1: add a fused `LogicalFns::and_popcnt_fn` in `gf2-kernels-simd` so the 512/1024 design sizes route through AVX2 while keeping unsafe code isolated in the SIMD kernel crate.

The accepted fix: for row width >= 8 u64 words (512 columns), `BitMatrix::matvec` calls `LogicalFns::and_popcnt_fn` once per row and uses the low bit of the popcount as the GF(2) dot-product parity. Below threshold, or without an available SIMD backend, it keeps the scalar fallback.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] Existing `matrix.rs` tests pass; new word-boundary `#[test]` for matvec passes at n in {0, 1, 63, 64, 65, 127, 128, 129}.
- [hard] Proptest equivalence vs. scalar holds for all sizes 0..1024 via the I4 helper.
- [hard] Crossover threshold documented in code with the bench data point that justifies it.
- [hard] Sibling `*.asm.txt` artefact regenerated and shows the approved fused `vpand` + popcount mnemonics (`vpshufb`, `vpsadbw`, `vpaddq`) in the dispatched call site.
- [hard] `perf stat -r 10` capture before/after recorded in this JIT issue.
- [aspirational] >= 1.5x geomean over baseline at design size class (matrices >= 512 x 512). Below the bar: revert and try a different transform; do not merge.

## Perf evidence

Criterion comparator on main after refreshing A1 leaves:

- Baseline: `ppc-v0-2026-04-27 @ 52eaac8`.
- `dense_matvec/512`: 4127.9 ns baseline, 1752.4 ns new, 2.356x speedup.
- `dense_matvec/1024`: 12796.5 ns baseline, 4339.5 ns new, 2.949x speedup.
- Geomean: 2.636x, target >= 1.5x, PASS.

`perf stat -r 10` before/after capture is recorded in `dev/benchmarks/jit-8e4b189c-matvec.txt`:

- Before 512: task-clock:u 1,646.72 msec (+- 9.62%); cycles 7,841,963,728; instructions 28,659,913,752; IPC 3.7; elapsed 1.648834236 +- 0.158433851 s.
- Before 1024: task-clock:u 1,799.87 msec (+- 1.79%); cycles 8,583,412,208; instructions 31,989,786,831; IPC 3.7; elapsed 1.802012654 +- 0.032136800 s.
- After 512: task-clock:u 1,931.52 msec (+- 0.22%); cycles 9,178,731,655; instructions 47,826,074,590; IPC 5.2; elapsed 1.933668333 +- 0.004307532 s.
- After 1024: task-clock:u 1,181.15 msec (+- 0.16%); cycles 5,585,455,595; instructions 28,810,989,455; IPC 5.2; elapsed 1.183225150 +- 0.001845080 s.

## Notes

Bench: `matrix_vector` (existing, pinned by I1). Implementation commit: `54c0a21 perf(jit:8e4b189c): route matvec through SIMD popcount`. Spec doc: `dev/plans/gf2_core_ppc_spiral.md`. Scope amendment approved by the user during lead review on 2026-04-28.
title: Route BitMatrix::matvec through popcnt SIMD dispatch
